questions.question: Why is cursor (keyset) pagination usually faster than offset pagination for deep pages?
options: It caches every page in memory
It seeks directly to the cursor row via an index, while OFFSET makes the database walk past all skipped rows
It skips the ORDER BY clause
It returns fewer columns per row
questions.explanation: OFFSET 100000 still reads and discards 100,000 rows. A cursor condition on an indexed, unique ordering lets the database jump straight to the next rows, so every page costs about the same.

questions.question: Why should the sort query parameter be checked against an allow-list before building orderBy?
options: Prisma cannot sort by more than one column
It prevents injection, sorting on private columns and slow sorts on unindexed columns
questions.explanation: Client input must never choose arbitrary columns. Mapping it to a fixed set of sortable fields keeps queries safe and predictable, and an unknown field returns 400.

questions.question: When implementing cursor pagination, why fetch take + 1 rows?
options: The extra row reveals whether another page exists, so nextCursor can be null on the last page
Prisma always drops the first row
It is required for the COUNT query to work
questions.explanation: If more than take rows come back there is a next page; the extra row is discarded and the last returned row's id becomes the cursor.

questions.question: Why add id as a secondary orderBy when sorting expenses by spentOn?
options: MySQL requires a primary key in every ORDER BY
It makes the query use less memory
Without a unique tie-breaker, rows with the same date can come back in any order, causing duplicates or gaps across pages
It sorts newest expenses first automatically
questions.explanation: Pagination needs a deterministic, total ordering. Adding a unique column like id breaks ties so each row appears on exactly one page.
